data.narrative:
Wisk Aero is a Series C-stage aerospace company that has raised $450M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 13 Space & Aerospace comparables—5 public and 8 private—including stage-adjacent and same-sector participants like Sierra Space, Impulse Space, and Apex Space.

Two methods triangulate the valuation. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $765M. Peer-median analysis examines 7 same-sector and same/adjacent-stage private comparables with valuations ranging from $1.15B to $8.0B; the median across this set is $2.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples is not applicable given the absence of disclosed revenue. The peer-median method carries greater weight given the breadth of the comparable set.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $650M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median estimate of $1.4B. This range reflects material uncertainty around stage-specific progression rates and peer comparability, particularly given the wide dispersion in the private peer set ($1.15B–$8.0B). The $2.0B peer-median sits at the upper end of this range, while the $765M stage-progression result anchors the lower bound. Key uncertainties include the target's underlying revenue trajectory, technical differentiation relative to Sierra Space and Impulse Space, and capital efficiency metrics versus the broader aerospace cohort.
